questions.question: During a basic vehicle controls skills test, where should your vehicle's final position be?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must finish in the exact position the examiner described. If you do not complete the exercise exactly as described, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, a school bus driver should wait for all surrounding traffic to stop before:

options.text: Opening the door and signaling students to approach.
Turning on the alternating red lights.
Pulling over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the door and signaling students to approach.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver must make sure all surrounding traffic has stopped before opening the door and signaling for students to approach the bus.

questions.question: Where are a school bus's danger zones located?

options.text: Only in front of the bus.
Only to the rear and left side of the bus.
In front, to the sides, and to the rear of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front, to the sides, and to the rear of the bus.
questions.explanation: Danger zones are areas where children are most likely to be hit by another vehicle or by the bus itself. These areas are in front, to the sides, and to the rear of the bus. Danger zones can extend 10 feet from every side of a bus.

questions.question: If a student has a suspected back injury, what should you do?

options.text: Move them off the bus.
Do not move them.
Encourage them to try to stand.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them.
questions.explanation: Do not move a student with a suspected neck or spinal injury unless their life is in immediate danger.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should check that:

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The pedal surfaces are not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces are not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that nothing blocks the pedals. Make sure the pedals work properly and the surfaces are grooved and not worn smooth.

questions.question: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must be completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Not use the mirrors.
Approach with caution.
Drive quickly and stop suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach with caution.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers should approach stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: During testing exercises (except straight line backing), how many times can a driver exit the vehicle to check its position?

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during basic vehicle control skills tests. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you can only look one time. For other exercises, you can look two times.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Honk the horn.
Drive slowly.
Talk to students on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly.
questions.explanation: Always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Who can change bus stops?

options.text: The driver.
Parents.
The school district.

questions.correctAnswerText: The school district.
questions.explanation: The school district establishes official bus routes and stops. Drivers must never change a stop location without written approval from a district official.

questions.question: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors allow you to see all of the following, except:

options.text: The right and left front tires touching the ground.
The area in front of the bus.
The tops of the right and left rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tops of the right and left rear tires.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors should help you see the area in front of the bus, from the front bumper at ground level to where you can see directly. They should also show the right and left front tires touching the ground and the area from the front of the bus to the service door.

questions.question: For a basic vehicle control skills test, you are expected to be able to:

options.text: Alley dock.
Weave between a line of cones.
Complete an emergency stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alley dock.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back parking on the right and left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, a look is when:

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on their instrument panel.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver walks to the back of their vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver walks to the back of their vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look happens when you open your door, get up from your seat, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check where it is. During straight line backing, you can only do one look. During any other exercise, you can do up to two looks.

questions.question: If a school bus stalls on a railroad track:

options.text: Students should remain on the bus.
Students should be evacuated to a location near the bus.
Students should be evacuated and moved away from the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should be evacuated and moved away from the bus.
questions.explanation: If the bus stalls or gets stuck on railroad tracks, evacuate everyone right away. Move students far away from the bus at an angle away from any oncoming trains to avoid debris if a train hits the bus.

questions.question: Loading and unloading a bus:

options.text: Can be hazardous for passengers.
Does not need to be supervised.
Should be done while refueling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be hazardous for passengers.
questions.explanation: More students are hurt or killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Drivers must follow safety procedures during loading and unloading.

questions.question: If there is a fire on a school bus, the students:

options.text: Must be evacuated.
Should stay on the bus but be moved to a part of the bus unaffected by the fire.
Should stay in their seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be evacuated.
questions.explanation: If the bus is on fire or might catch fire, you must get all students off the bus right away.

questions.question: If a bus must be evacuated, it is safest for students to:

options.text: Stand no more than 50 feet away from the bus.
Stand downwind of the bus in the event of a fire.
Be led far away from any railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be led far away from any railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: After evacuating, move students to a safe place at least 100 feet from the road toward oncoming traffic. This protects them from debris if another vehicle hits the bus. Keep them upwind from fires and as far as possible from railroad tracks.

questions.question: After students unload at the school, a driver should:

options.text: Not be concerned with the students' whereabouts.
Leave after the students have entered the school building.
Walk through the bus to check for any sleeping students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for any sleeping students.
questions.explanation: After students unload at school, walk through the bus to check for sleeping students, students hiding, and items left behind. Make sure students exit in an orderly way while you supervise.

questions.question: If exiting a bus, a driver must:

options.text: Never make contact with the handrail.
Maintain contact with the handrail.
Move quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain contact with the handrail.
questions.explanation: When exiting the vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If it is a bus, keep holding the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: When students board a bus, they should:

options.text: Sit in the back row first.
Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
Be seated as far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
questions.explanation: Students should not sit in the back row unless the bus is full. Students are safer when seated closer to the front in case of a rear-end crash. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.
